rationale: The critical path (Q of _394_ through or4/nor4/nor4b/or4b/o41ai/and3/a22o back to D of _394_) runs entirely through the state-transition case statement's decode logic. The RTL only carries a plain `// synopsys full_case parallel_case` comment, which Yosys does not interpret as a synthesis directive, so the mutually-exclusive one-hot case arms get elaborated with an implicit priority order and ABC maps that into a long serial chain of wide gates instead of a flat select. Replacing the dead comment with a genuine Yosys `(* parallel_case *)` attribute on both case statements tells the tool what is already structurally true (every arm compares c_state, or cmd, against a distinct constant, so at most one ever matches), removing the artificial priority dependency between arms without adding any new don't-cares: unmatched state codes still fall through and hold their previous value exactly as before, so the function is unchanged for every input including unreachable ones. This lets synthesis rebalance the decode into a shallower, more parallel structure, directly shortening the reported depth-dominated path.
